name: Snapcase
label: Victory Records
lede: A West Seneca basement band cut its first single with a Goo Goo Doll, made a hardcore record Turnstile still points to, and quit when it felt like flogging a dead horse.

eras.title: Solid State in a West Seneca basement
eras.text: Four Buffalo-suburb teenagers, the youngest 15, started a band called Solid State and burned through singers and drummers across four demos. By 1992 it was Snapcase, on Victory Records, with its bassist moving to the mic.

years.h: Solid State starts in a basement in West Seneca, New York
years.p: Guitarist Scott Dressler is 15, drummer Mike Kimaid 17, bassist Daryl Taberski 18 and singer Tiger Balduf 19. The band that becomes Snapcase is born outside Buffalo.

years.h: Solid State cuts its first demo, Quest for Reality
years.p: Tiger Balduf and Mike Kimaid are already gone before the tape rolls. Chris Galas sings and Peter Dawidzik drums.
years.xp: On May 22, 1990 a second demo, Accept Your Fate, was recorded with Mike Lampe, with Galas, Dressler, Taberski and Jason Kourkounis on drums.

years.h: Solid State becomes Snapcase, a five-piece
years.p: Jason Kourkounis leaves, Mike Kimaid comes back on drums and Joe Smith of The Watchmen adds a second guitar. The new name is Snapcase, and two more demos follow with Dennis Fura.

years.h: Snapcase signs to Victory and records Comatose with Robby Takac
years.p: Chicago's Victory Records signs Snapcase. The first 7" is recorded with Mike Sac and Buffalo's own Robby Takac of the Goo Goo Dolls.

years.h: Daryl Taberski moves from bass to vocals as Chris Galas leaves
years.p: After the Comatose single, Taberski takes over the mic. Bob Whiteside and Jon Salemi arrive from the Buffalo band Support, on bass and guitar.

eras.title: Lookinglasself and the California Takeover
eras.text: Snapcase made its first album with New York hardcore's go-to engineer, lost a drummer mid-session and found a permanent one from a Buffalo band Scott Vogel had fronted. By 1996 it was touring as part of Victory's roster package with Earth Crisis and Strife.

years.h: Lookinglasself, Snapcase's first album, with Don Fury
years.p: Recorded with Don Fury and Fred Betschen. Drummer Mike Kimaid quits partway through and Timothy Redmond, formerly of Slugfest, finishes the drum tracks.
years.xp: Slugfest was the early-90s Buffalo band co-founded by [[Scott Vogel|4ab1b4fb-f2fe-458c-a496-0de55c7bf3cb]], who went on to front [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]]. Redmond stayed Snapcase's drummer until 2002.

years.h: Fields of Illusion on Victory's Only the Strong
years.p: Snapcase's track sits on Victory Records' 1993 label compilation, beside [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and the rest of the label's early roster.

years.h: Steps EP, Scott Dressler's last Snapcase record
years.p: Recorded with Fred Betschen. It's the final recording for founding guitarist Scott Dressler.

years.h: Scott Dressler leaves for grad school; Frank Vicario joins
years.p: Dressler goes on to become an economics professor at Villanova University. Vicario comes over from the Buffalo band Fadeaway.

years.h: The California Takeover with Earth Crisis and Strife
years.p: Victory Records releases a live album splitting a California night between Snapcase, [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]].

eras.title: Two weeks and a case of chickenpox
eras.text: Progression Through Unlearning was recorded fast, sick and young, and barely reviewed. It's now the Snapcase record that 2020s bands like Turnstile, Higher Power and Drug Church name, and it put the band on Warped Tour and in front of Deftones crowds.

years.h: Progression Through Unlearning, made in two weeks
years.p: Recorded in January 1997 with Steve Evetts at Trax East in New Jersey, with guitarist Jon Salemi playing through chickenpox. The band later said the recording and mastering were rushed.
years.xp:
Few outlets reviewed it at the time. Vice later called it Snapcase's timeless hardcore classic, and Wikipedia credits it with pointing toward 2000s metalcore and with the melodic hardcore revival, citing Turnstile, Higher Power and Drug Church as bands that named it.

Two songs were co-written by the departed Scott Dressler.

years.h: Snapcase plays the Vans Warped Tour
years.p: Snapcase takes Progression Through Unlearning onto the 1997 Warped Tour. That fall the members take time off for school.

years.h: Snapcase opens for Deftones and Quicksand
years.p: Snapcase opens the fall 1998 Deftones and [[Quicksand|3c9f8bef-a658-4204-9ee8-7e95d2535b32]] tour, and cuts [[Bad Brains|e919b253-da5b-4aae-a444-6a368376a2d6]]' I with Brian McTernan for the tribute Never Give In.

years.h: Split 7" with Boysetsfire, then Bob Whiteside leaves
years.p: Energy Dome backs [[Boysetsfire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]]'s Truth Hits Everybody. It's bassist Whiteside's last record; Dustin Perry of Minnesota's Threadbare replaces him.

years.h: Snapcase headlines Hellfest in Syracuse
years.p: Snapcase tops the bill at the Syracuse, New York hardcore festival Hellfest.

eras.title: Designs, transmissions and a dead horse
eras.text: Snapcase went further out, onto Warped's main stage and a European tour with NOFX, while the hardcore audience that loved Progression drifted. By late 2004 the band called it.

years.h: Designs for Automotion, with Steve Evetts again
years.p: Snapcase's third album was recorded in summer 1999 with Evetts and released at the start of 2000.

years.h: Europe with NOFX and the Warped main stage
years.p: Snapcase plays Europe on the Deconstruction tour with [[NOFX|dcaa4f81-bfb7-44eb-8594-4e74f004b6e4]] and moves up to the Vans Warped Tour main stage.

years.h: Ben Lythberg drums while Timothy Redmond finishes a master's
years.p: Lythberg covers from fall 2000 to spring 2001.

years.h: Breaking and Reaching soundtracks Toonami's Gundam promos
years.p: Cartoon Network's Toonami uses the Snapcase song for its Mobile Fighter G Gundam promos.

years.h: End Transmission at Salad Days Studios
years.p: Brian McTernan records Snapcase's fourth album. Afterwards Timothy Redmond leaves for good and Ben Lythberg becomes the drummer.

years.h: On tour with Boysetsfire and a young Atreyu
years.p: Snapcase takes out [[Boysetsfire|ba561cc7-2050-47d3-8bc2-c645a1393d90]] and [[Atreyu|17e137fb-59e5-4fd7-af48-afc34995396c]], then Victory's rising metalcore band.

years.h: Bright Flashes: covers, remixes, Devo and Helmet
years.p: Snapcase's last release gathers songs from the End Transmission concept, remixes and covers of Helmet, Devo and Jane's Addiction.
years.xp: That spring Snapcase opened for Bad Religion and Finch and made its last trip abroad.

q: tough to keep flogging a dead horse when hearts are in other places
years.h: Snapcase announces it's breaking up
years.p: The band's statement admits its popularity has been waning. Frank Vicario says fans rejected the newer direction and came with fixed ideas of what Snapcase should sound like.
years.xp: Punknews ran the news with a farewell show promised for January in Buffalo. Some members started a project called Ourselves.

years.h: Snapcase's final show in Buffalo brings back the old members
years.p: Nearly every former member turns up, among them Timothy Redmond, Scott Dressler, Bob Whiteside and Chris Galas.
years.xp: After the split Redmond taught at Williamsville East High School, and Vicario, Perry and Lythberg formed the band Attractive with Josh English of Sixgoingonseven.

eras.title: Buffalo keeps calling them back
eras.text: Snapcase never fully reunited, but it keeps coming back for the right causes and anniversaries. A volcano grounded one comeback; the 25th birthday filled the Town Ballroom.

years.h: Snapcase reunites at Mohawk Place in Buffalo
years.p: Snapcase's first show since 2005, followed on November 24 and 25 by two nights at Brooklyn's Music Hall of Williamsburg.
years.xp: The Brooklyn shows were a benefit for Callum Robbins and doubled as the release party for the Anti-Matter Anthology book.

years.h: An Icelandic volcano cancels Snapcase's European return
years.p: The Eyjafjallajökull ash cloud grounds flights and wipes out Snapcase's April dates, including Belgium's Groezrock. The band reschedules for July.

years.h: Snapcase and Sick of It All in Buffalo
years.p: Snapcase plays a hometown reunion show with [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]], then Chicago's Riot Fest and Austin's Fun Fun Fun Fest later in 2010.

years.h: Sick of It All's 25th anniversary at Webster Hall
years.p: Snapcase supports [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]] at the New York band's anniversary show.

years.h: Snapcase at the tenth This Is Hardcore
years.p: The band plays Philadelphia's This Is Hardcore festival at Union Transfer.

years.h: Snapcase's 25th anniversary show at Buffalo's Town Ballroom
years.p: Twenty-five years after Solid State became Snapcase, the band celebrates at home.

years.h: The Return of the California Takeover
years.p: Snapcase, [[Earth Crisis|88a6037e-87ba-492a-a54c-c927aa620cb8]] and [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] share a record again, 25 years after the original.

years.h: Snapcase covers Refused for The Shape of Punk to Come Obliterated
years.p: Snapcase takes on [[Refused|42884e27-dfb8-453d-990f-2ffd90bc2d1a]]' Summer Holidays vs. Punkroutine for the tribute, and plays Far Out, Bro on And Now I'm Just Gnashing My Teeth.

q: we wouldn't exist as a band if it wasn't for them
years.h: Snapcase covers Zero Tolerance's Back to Square One
years.p: Recorded for Iodine Recordings' animal-shelter benefit The Dogs of Hope. Daryl Taberski calls Zero Tolerance the forefathers of Buffalo hardcore.
years.xp: Profits went to the Randolph County Animal Shelter in Wedowee, Alabama. Zero Tolerance flyers were among the first Scott Vogel ever picked up, at a D.R.I. show in Buffalo.
